style.vernacular: Caribbean grid town rebuilt after the great fire of 1867: two- and three-storey Georgian-style masonry-and-timber buildings with stone or stuccoed ground floors, timber upper floors, verandahs and fretwork balconies, hipped roofs of red or grey corrugated metal, pastel and cream paint; low painted-concrete blocks outside the centre; volcanic grey stone for forts; palms and flamboyant trees against steep green hills.
style.ornament: Timber fretwork and balcony railings on upper galleries; Georgian sash and louvred shutters; cast-iron Victorian fountain at The Circus (1883) modelled on Piccadilly Circus; stone quoins and arched ground-floor openings; contrast white trim on pastel walls.

sources.what: buildings largely rebuilt after the 1867 fire; The Circus with 1883 fountain; Independence Square with cathedral and courthouse; grid layout
